title: What If the British Never Came?

beats.text: What if British never touch *India?*
The honest answer is not the *fairy tale* you were expecting.
In 1700, India made *a quarter* of everything produced on Earth.
By 1950, around *4%.*
That's the part everybody knows.
Here's the part people *skip.*
Britain didn't defeat a *strong, united* India.
In 1757, Clive had *3,000* men against *50,000.*
He won by *buying* the enemy commander.
India, in 1750, was already *cracked open.*
*Nadir Shah* had just robbed Delhi.
The *Marathas* had just been crushed at *Panipat.*
Dozens of kingdoms were *hungry* for money and weapons.
So no, Britain does not automatically mean a *rich, free* India.
It might mean someone else walks through that *unlocked door.*
But Bengal would not have lost *a third* of its people in 1770, while tax collectors kept collecting,
and Indian cloth would not have priced out by factories running on *Indian cotton.*
So the real question is whether India would have been *richer.*
It's whether it would even be *one country,*
because the India we know was *forged* in resistance to the Raj.
Remove the enemy, and you might remove the *glue.*
*Comment* what you think happens.
